skill.name: set-up-shopify-google-ads-enhanced-conversions
skill.description: Set up or troubleshoot Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for Shopify through Product Metrics. Check server-side tracking, consent settings, and Google customer data terms, then verify setup with a paid test order.
skill.summary: Check and verify Shopify Enhanced Conversions for Google Ads with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most matches are documentation, scoped status checks, or ordinary vendor links, not system reconnaissance or backtick execution. Risks include broad order lookups, unpinned installation, unsafe credential handling, setup beyond the requested scope, and reliance on live instructions. No evidence found of prompt injection, malicious exfiltration, or deliberate consent bypass.

remediation.issue: The workflow allows credentials for unrelated integrations to be passed to commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove these exceptions from the Shopify workflow. Use provider authorization or a dedicated secret input that keeps credentials out of chat, process arguments, and logs.

remediation.issue: Order diagnostics can retrieve real orders and business details beyond the requested setup check.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer tracking status checks. If order access is necessary, confirm the storefront and use the explicit test order ID. Report only the relevant status.

remediation.issue: The optional installer does not pin the launcher or the community skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Use a reviewed launcher version and an immutable skill revision. Keep installation a separate action that requires explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: The prerequisite workflow can expand into unrelated ad channels and paid setup.
remediation.suggestion: Stop after reporting missing prerequisites. Get separate approval for store links, permissions, billing, consent settings, or conversion actions before proceeding. Exclude unrelated destinations.

remediation.issue: The fallback treats live remote documentation as equivalent to the reviewed local instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed instructions. Treat live documentation as reference material only, and do not let it expand tool permissions or authorize changes.

content.user_title: Set Up Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for Shopify
content.value_statement: Google Ads can miss Shopify purchases when click tracking alone cannot match them. Use Product Metrics to verify consent, Google account readiness, and tracking for a paid test order.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP server when you provide authorized access.
Check whether server-side tracking and Product Metrics conversion actions are in place.
Guide you to select the consent banner your Shopify storefront uses.
Explain Google customer data terms and Data Manager acceptance statuses.
Guide you through a paid test order and explain the tracking check results.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics and existing Shopify server-side tracking for Google Ads. Its app steps can guide you when tool access is unavailable.
An authorized user must complete Shopify and Google Ads approvals, including customer data terms.
This workflow does not manage Customer Match, change bidding, or make conversion actions primary.
A passing test does not guarantee that Google matches every order to an ad click.

use_cases.title: Check Readiness Before Setup
use_cases.description: Identify which Product Metrics and Google Ads prerequisites are already complete before changing anything.

use_cases.title: Diagnose an Acceptance Problem
use_cases.description: Distinguish missing customer data terms from a Data Manager rejection and identify the next step for the account admin.

use_cases.title: Verify One Client Store
use_cases.description: Check a selected store and Google Ads account, then record consent and tracking test results without sharing customer details.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review prerequisites before making changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my Shopify store is ready for Enhanced Conversions in Google Ads. List any missing prerequisites without changing settings.

prompt_templates.title: Verify the Consent Banner
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Confirm the selected banner matches the storefront.
prompt_templates.prompt: My Shopify store uses Cookiebot. Tell me where to confirm the banner in Product Metrics and explain which consent controls each type of data.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Data Manager Rejection
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Find the right action for the Google Ads admin.
prompt_templates.prompt: Product Metrics shows Data Manager acceptance as Rejected. Explain what the Google Ads admin should check and how to verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Tracking Without Changing Bidding
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review one client account and test order.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review consent, customer data terms, and tracking for this Shopify store and Google Ads client account. Use only my designated paid test order. Keep the review read-only and report any remaining manual checks.

output_examples.input: Product Metrics says the customer data terms are not accepted. What should I do?
output_examples.output: In Product Metrics, open Tracking, then Google Ads. Under Enhanced conversions, select Open Google Ads settings. Ask the Google Ads admin to review and accept the terms, then select Re-check in Product Metrics.

output_examples.input: Enhanced Conversions says Ready. How do I test it?
output_examples.output: Place and pay for a designated test order. In the Shopify app, open Tracking and select Run tracking test. Look for Passing and Tracking is live on your store. These checks do not prove that Google attributed the order to an ad.

best_practices: Confirm the Shopify store, Product Metrics workspace, and Google Ads client account before using connected tools.
Verify that Configure consent names the banner actually shown on the store.
Use a designated paid test order and report only the tracking status, not customer details.
anti_patterns: Changing consent settings to force data through when a visitor declined.
Pasting customer records, passwords, or API credentials into the conversation.
Treating a passing tracking test as a reason to change primary conversions or bidding.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. This workflow uses Product Metrics and assumes server-side conversion tracking is already configured for the connected Shopify store and Google Ads account.

faq.question: Do I need Google Tag Manager?
faq.answer: No. This workflow sends eligible conversion data through Google Data Manager and does not require changing a Google tag.

faq.question: Which customer fields can Google Ads receive?
faq.answer: With ad user data consent, Product Metrics can send hashed email, phone, and name. For the name fields, it also sends country and postcode without hashing them.

faq.question: What happens when a visitor declines ad user data?
faq.answer: If they allow ad storage, Google Ads can receive the order conversion without the hashed customer data. If they decline both, the order is not sent.

faq.question: Who accepts the Google customer data terms?
faq.answer: A Google Ads admin accepts them in Google Ads. If Product Metrics says a manager account controls the terms, the admin must accept them there.

faq.question: Why does Product Metrics still say Setting up?
faq.answer: Data Manager can take about 15 minutes to recognize new conversion actions. Select Re-check after waiting and review any action that Product Metrics lists.
